fixes.explanation: Close, but the rule doesn't run on one witness. Paul quotes it like this: “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.” The rule asks for two or three, never just one. I'd be nervous if my whole case rested on one guy saying, "Trust me, I saw it."

That's the opposite of what Paul writes. He warns “…those who sinned earlier and everyone else…” and then says, “If I return, I will not spare anyone…” He names the ones who sinned earlier, and he names everyone else right alongside them. Nobody gets a pass. I think anyone reading that line sits up a little straighter.

That one's not in these verses. Peter was one of Jesus' apostles (Matthew 10:2), but Paul never mentions him here. What the Corinthians are demanding is “…proof that Christ is speaking through me.” They want to know whose voice is behind Paul's words, and Peter never comes up.

That's the second blank, and it's a good one. “…He lives by God’s power.” The same sentence that says weakness says power, and that's what Paul wants them to hear. In that very verse he adds that he and his companions are weak in Him, yet by God’s power they will live with Him concerning the Corinthians.

That's pointing the clipboard at somebody else, friend. Paul tells them to “Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith…” The check is about themselves, not about their leaders. It's a lot easier to inspect somebody else's oven than your own.

That's the word, baker. Paul writes, “…we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong…” He says his group is weak, and they rejoice when the Corinthians are strong. That's a leader cheering from the back of the room, and I love it.

Quiet doesn't fit this sentence. Paul says, “…we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong…” The contrast he makes is weak and strong. A strong church is probably a lot of things, but Paul never says quiet.

That's it, baker. Paul closes with “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.” The Lord Jesus Christ, God and the Holy Spirit are all named in one line. What a way to end a letter.

Close in sound, but not in the text. Paul's last line names “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit…” The apostles aren't mentioned there. The third one is the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.
